# SEAMS.md — Knauf Upstream Modifications

## Upstream Base

| Field         | Value               |
| ------------- | ------------------- |
| LibreChat tag | `v0.8.7`            |
| Base tag      | `knauf/base-v0.8.7` |
| Last synced   | 2026-05-07          |

The `LibreChat tag` row is the upstream baseline used by [`upstream-release-watcher.yml`](.github/workflows/upstream-release-watcher.yml) to compute `upstream/<base>..upstream/<latest>` diffs. It must be a real tag in `danny-avila/LibreChat`. The `Base tag` row is the Knauf-side anchor used by humans to identify the merge commit on the fork.

## Inline Modifications

> **Append-only.** Each ticket appends its own row(s); prior rows are never edited. A single upstream file may appear in multiple rows, one per ticket that touched it. The `Ticket` column carries the originating Jira ID (`KK20-XXX`), or `—` for rows that predate the convention. `Lines` is captured at the commit that added the seam; drift after subsequent reformats is accepted. See [.claude/skills/seam-manifest/SKILL.md](.claude/skills/seam-manifest/SKILL.md).

| `knauf/scripts/seed-agent-builder-role.js`                                                                  | KK20-243 — grants the AGENT_BUILDER role `SKILLS: {USE: true, CREATE: false, SHARE: false, SHARE_PUBLIC: false}`; it was hard-set all-false, so enabling the skills capability would still have left AI Champions with no `$` popover, no composer chip and no sidebar catalog. CREATE stays false because authoring belongs to platform engineering, matching `interface.skills`. This must stay explicit: the script does `$set: { permissions }`, a full replace, and `updateInterfacePermissions` only ever iterates USER and ADMIN, so nothing else writes SKILLS onto this role and a missing permission type reads as deny. Operationally it is neither a job nor a migration — a human runs it via mongosh per environment after each release, and running an older checkout afterwards silently reverts SKILLS to false. Also adds a `/* global db, printjson */` directive and a `prettier-ignore` over the aligned PERMISSIONS table so the file passes the pre-commit gates it had never been staged against.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

Its absence did not mean off: `resolveSummarizationConfig` tests `config?.enabled !== false`, so `undefined !== false` had summarization enabled by accident. Four contradictions found by an adversarial pass over the full instruction surface and fixed here. **(1)** The `Artifacts:` paragraph said "follow them exactly" about `generateArtifactsPrompt`, which says "Prefer in-line content (don't use artifacts) when possible" (`prompts/artifacts/index.ts:219`) and "err on the side of not creating an artifact" (`:284`) — and lands AFTER the anchor in the same system message, so it won on both deference and recency. Now a positive imperative tied to a checkable precondition (loaded instructions → the reply must contain the artifact), with carve-outs for prior-turn artifacts and for when the user asked for the plan itself. | `librechat.yaml` · `skill/karl-artifacts/references/*.md` · `skill/karl-brand/SKILL.md`                     | KK20-252 (fifth append for this ticket) — artifact-body emission discipline, after KARL shipped a deck whose file carried, after the component's closing brace, an HTML comment, prose, and mangled backtick fences; Sandpack threw `Unexpected token (97:0)` on the `<!-- -->`. The HTML comment was **displacement caused by the fourth append**: upstream orders the model to announce shadcn/ui (`packages/api/src/prompts/artifacts/index.ts:277`), that append banned saying it _in a reply_, and the model satisfied both by hiding it in a comment inside the file. Fixed by scoping the ban to audience rather than surface, and by three carve-outs an adversarial pass caught in the first attempt: `text/markdown` artifacts are prose end to end so a blanket no-prose rule would have broken them; the `KNAUF` block karl-brand orders transcribed verbatim is half comments, several load-bearing, so a blanket no-comment rule would have stripped them; and `Say nothing, anywhere` about libraries would have reached the `import` lines themselves, pushing the model to hand-roll primitives out of raw divs. Also adds the column-0 rule — the upstream format example is indented 6 spaces, and at 4+ spaces CommonMark takes the block as indented code so the directive never parses and the artifact lands in chat with no error — plus a ban on using a placeholder image for the Knauf mark and on the self-deprecating commentary upstream invites. The skill edits strip skill names and file paths from comment lines inside copy-verbatim blocks, which the new ban would otherwise have made unfollowable on its first real use. Guarded by three new cases in `librechatYaml.knauf.spec.ts`                                                                                                                           |

KARL had emitted `import { useKnaufTheme, KNAUF } from '/knauf-brand-tokens'` — a module that did not exist — after earlier turns produced placeholder logos and trimmed token blocks; the model was routing around a design that asked it to retype 903 characters of coordinate data whose own reference says "any edit silently deforms the letterforms, and there is no error to tell you". Skills: `karl-brand/SKILL.md` now states the React path is an import and scopes transcription to media with no module system (HTML/SVG artifacts, documents, decks, email); its `KNAUF` block **stays** — it is where the values are authored, `references/non-artifact.md` still needs them, and removing it would strand four hexes that only exist there and in karl-artifacts' quick-card mirror, failing `deploymentSkills.knauf.spec.ts`'s hex guard. `karl-artifacts/SKILL.md` gains `/knauf/brand` in the import allowlist and loses the flat "no importing your own modules" prohibition that directly forbade it. The three layout templates open with the import instead of a paste preamble. `references/logo.md` keeps its raw-SVG block for the types that cannot import and drops the duplicate React copy — hence `toHaveLength(2)` → `toHaveLength(1)` in that spec. `librechat.yaml`: two clauses only. "import freely from everything available to you" → bounded to "the paths and libraries your artifact instructions list" (the unbounded grant is the plausible source of the invented path), and the wordmark sentence now names the import for React while keeping inline SVG for every other type. The shadcn files were mounted the whole time; the model wrote a barrel import that is not mounted, and `TabList`, which is not an export (shadcn's is `TabsList`). **Root cause is ours, not upstream's.** `karl-artifacts/SKILL.md` recommended `Card`, `Tabs`, `Table` and `Badge` by name while carrying an import example for only Card and Table (in the report and dashboard templates). The specs run `artifacts: 'default'`, which omits `generateShadcnPrompt` and therefore the whole `components.ts` manifest — so for `Tabs` and `Badge` the model had a recommendation, the bare pattern `/components/ui/<name>`, and nothing else. It extrapolated. `'shadcnui'` was tried and reverted: it fixes the symptom by shipping a 711-line catalogue of all 37 components at ~2.9k tokens/turn, to support the four the skill actually recommends. The fix is the skill carrying those four import lines with their real export names, plus a note that there is no barrel. Two guards, both negative-tested: `deploymentSkills.knauf.spec.ts` fails if any recommended component has no import example (naming `Tabs` and `Badge` when the block is removed) or if any skill points at the barrel; `librechatYaml.knauf.spec.ts` pins the mode, so flipping to `'shadcnui'` is a visible decision rather than a silent one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

| `.github/workflows/promote_pipeline.yaml` | KK20-195 — fixes a false-positive "Current STAGE app revisions differ from E2E provenance" failure. `agk-deployment-configs` is a shared monorepo, so ArgoCD reports the whole-repo branch HEAD as the STAGE app's `sync.revision`; any unrelated commit elsewhere in the repo (e.g. bumping dev's tag or another service's config) advanced that SHA and tripped the strict equality check even though nothing under the STAGE app/worker config paths had changed. The drift check now compares the sha256 content hash of the live `values.yaml` at the current STAGE app/worker paths against the provenance-recorded hashes instead of requiring exact whole-repo revision equality, and the equivalent raw-SHA check on the worker ArgoCD app was removed for the same reason. |
| `.github/workflows/promote_pipeline.yaml` | KK20-195 — moves "Deploy Stage to Prod" onto its own concurrency group (`${{ github.repository }}-promote`) instead of sharing `${{ github.repository }}-release` with `release_pipeline.yaml`. Previously, any merge to `main` (which auto-triggers `release_pipeline.yaml`) queued a running/pending prod promotion behind it, since both used the same group. Release Pipeline only touches nonprod (dev) ACR/ArgoCD resources, so there is no shared-resource reason to serialize it with the prod promotion; the two now run independently. |
| `.github/workflows/release_pipeline.yaml` | KK20-195 — continuous delivery to stage: once the existing DEV health smoke passes, the release pipeline now automatically imports the exact dev image digest into stage's ACR namespace, bumps stage's GitOps config (app + worker tags) via an auto-merged PR (reusing the dev bump's auto-merge-PR idiom), and waits for stage ArgoCD to report Synced/Healthy — all in new steps ("Import exact dev image into AGK stage ACR namespace", "Update AGK stage deployment config values", "Refresh AGK stage ArgoCD application"). A "Run STAGE E2E (informational, non-gating)" step then dispatches `stage-e2e.yaml` in `agentic-karl-quality` for early-warning visibility only (`continue-on-error: true`; failures surface as a `::warning::` and a step-summary row, never fail the release job). This E2E run does **not** gate anything and does **not** produce a provenance artifact — per the agreed design, `promote_pipeline.yaml` (Pipeline 2) always re-runs STAGE E2E fresh immediately before any prod promotion, so that is the only real gate to prod. |
| `.github/workflows/deploy_stage_pipeline.yaml` (removed) | KK20-195 — **file deleted.** The pipeline is now exactly 2 workflows, not 3: `release_pipeline.yaml` (auto dev deploy + auto continuous delivery to stage + informational E2E) and `promote_pipeline.yaml` (the sole manual gate to prod). This workflow's stage-deploy logic — import the exact dev image digest into stage's ACR namespace, bump stage's GitOps config (app + worker tags) via an auto-merged PR, wait for stage ArgoCD Synced/Healthy — was fully inlined into `release_pipeline.yaml`'s new post-dev-smoke steps (see the row above); its STAGE E2E dispatch became `release_pipeline.yaml`'s "Run STAGE E2E (informational, non-gating)" step. Its optional-k6-profiles step and the "Record immutable STAGE validation provenance" step + `stage-validation-provenance-*` artifact upload were **not** carried forward anywhere — nothing downstream consumes them anymore, since `promote_pipeline.yaml` now snapshots and re-validates STAGE live instead of trusting an old run's artifact (see below). There is no longer any manual "deploy an explicit version to stage" workflow; stage always tracks whatever is on dev, deployed automatically by `release_pipeline.yaml`. |
| `.github/workflows/promote_pipeline.yaml` | KK20-195 — replaces the "trust an old `deploy_stage_pipeline.yaml` run's provenance artifact" model (that workflow is now deleted — see above) with live before/after snapshot verification, since Pipeline 1 (`release_pipeline.yaml`) now auto-deploys every release to stage and Pipeline 2 is the only gate to prod. Removed entirely: the `stage_run_id` input, the "Resolve STAGE run ID" step (added in PR #288 — history kept, logic not carried forward since there is no longer an old run to resolve), and "Validate trusted STAGE run and provenance" (downloaded/validated a `stage-validation-provenance-*` artifact from a `deploy_stage_pipeline.yaml` run). New flow: "Determine version to promote" now derives the version directly from what's currently live on stage's GitOps tag (an explicit `version` input is still accepted but must match); "Snapshot STAGE state (before E2E)" captures image digest, both git revisions (app + GitOps), and content-hash of the app+worker `values.yaml` directly from ArgoCD/ACR (same content-hash pattern as the old, now-removed provenance-recording step); "Run STAGE E2E tests" dispatches `stage-e2e.yaml` fresh, live, every time this pipeline runs (never reused/skipped); "Snapshot STAGE state (after E2E) and verify no drift" re-captures the identical fields and fails the job with a clear error if anything drifted (image digest, git revisions, config content hashes, or runtime digests) — protecting against promoting a version that was redeployed during/after its own test run. The content-hash-based drift-check approach (vs. brittle whole-repo git-SHA equality) is brought forward from open PR #290, which is not yet merged. The existing prod-promotion steps (ACR import/lock, GitOps bump, ArgoCD refresh, PROD health smoke) are unchanged, only now sourced from the before-snapshot's outputs instead of a downloaded provenance file. |
| `.github/workflows/{release_pipeline,promote_pipeline}.yaml` | KK20-195 — superseded by the rows above: the earlier rows describing `promote_pipeline.yaml`'s now-removed `stage_run_id` auto-resolve (PR #288) and its now-removed provenance/drift-check-by-artifact model no longer reflect current behavior, and `deploy_stage_pipeline.yaml` no longer exists at all (fully absorbed into `release_pipeline.yaml`, not merely repurposed). Kept in the manifest for history; see the KK20-195 rows above for the current 2-workflow design. |

| `knauf/brand/{logos,colours,guidelines,fonts}/**`                                 | KK20-243 — the source-of-truth Knauf brand kit as delivered (17 files, ~26 MB: EPS and PNG logos for both the primary KNAUF and the Knauf Insulation sub-brand, the official colour system as HTML plus a print PDF, the visual-identity guidelines PDF, and a licensed font archive). **Reference only** — excluded from the Docker build context by `.dockerignore`, so nothing here is reachable at runtime, and a sandboxed artifact preview can load neither a binary asset nor a network request. Runtime assets are exported into `client/public/assets/` and tracked as their own rows above; the palette and wordmark that artifacts need are transcribed as text into `skill/karl-brand/`.
